clue.text: Crushes MPs and later gets set right

indicators.note: to set something right is to put it in order, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Parliamentarians and later arrivals are put straight after some crushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set right' is the anagram signal working on MPS plus LATER; 'gets' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to stamp heavily on something, crushing it underfoot.

clue.text: Reptilian creature mocked by Lewis Carroll!

definitions.text: Reptilian creature mocked by Lewis Carroll!

parts.words: Reptilian creature mocked by Lewis Carroll!
parts.note: points to the sad Mock creature in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, read as one Carroll mocked

explanation.surface: A reptile ridiculed by the author of Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: Carroll's Mock Turtle is a creature, not mocked; the clue plays on 'mocked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelled reptile, and half the name of Carroll's Mock character in Alice.

clue.text: Look for a soft fruit

parts.note: p is piano, soft in music
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Searching for a squashy piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to look or seem, as in 'look tired'.

clue.text: In Scotland by the end of the month

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
the last two letters of month

explanation.surface: Something due in Scotland by the month's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Scotland' looks like a setting but defines a Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Perth is a city in central Scotland on the Tay.

clue.text: Regards a foreign coin as an unacceptable thing

parts.note: eyes as a verb means looks at, regards
the ore is a Scandinavian coin

explanation.surface: Someone treats a foreign coin as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly, unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: It's unfortunate about everything going for a song

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for unfortunate goes around the other piece

parts.note: unfortunate as in bad luck: bad
everything means all

explanation.surface: Someone laments that everything is being sold off for a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going for a song' suggests selling cheaply, but 'song' is the definition and 'going for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or slow sentimental tune.

clue.text: His is damp rotten at the centre

indicators.note: rotten suggests decay breaking these letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's damp timbers have rotted through in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' is the anagram signal working on HIS IS DAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle of a vessel, at its centre.

clue.text: Scholars are not all polite, rating it effete

indicators.note: only part of these words is used, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Scholars are snobbishly dismissed as effete by a polite critic.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are learned, well-read people.

clue.text: Getting into gear

parts.note: sounds like starting up a car but means putting on clothes

explanation.surface: Starting a car or machine moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear means clothes, so getting into it is putting clothes on.

clue.text: Told about taking wine in the tall grass

indicators.note: in means the wine word sits inside the grass word here

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in wet places
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A tale about drinking wine while hiding in tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told about something in a report is to have it related, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: "—— is like a rich stone, best plain set" Bacon (Essays)

definitions.text: "—— is like a rich stone, best plain set" Bacon (Essays)

parts.words: "—— is like a rich stone, best plain set" Bacon (Essays)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word opens a line from Francis Bacon's essay Of Beauty

explanation.surface: A quotation from Bacon's Essays comparing a moral quality to an unadorned gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon's essay Of Beauty opens with this line; the missing word is a moral quality, not beauty itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon's line likens moral goodness to a gem that looks best in a plain setting.

clue.text: Information from all quarters

parts.note: north is N, one of the four compass quarters
east is E
west is W
south is S

explanation.surface: Gathering information from every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings and reports are information.

clue.text: Nauseating decoration in a hotel's unusual

indicators.note: in means the decoration is placed inside the shuffled letters
unusual signals that the letters of a and hotel's appear in an unusual order

parts.note: the word hotel with its S counted as a letter
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A complaint that the hotel's decor is unusually sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges A HOTELS into LOATHSE; 'in' puts OM inside it, before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome provokes disgust, as does something nauseating.

clue.text: The school head remains to arrange classes

indicators.note: the head of the word school is its first letter

parts.note: orts are scraps of food left over, remains

explanation.surface: The headteacher stays behind to organise the timetable of classes.
explanation.walkthrough: ORTS, scraps left after a meal, is an old word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Classes in the sense of kinds or categories are sorts.

clue.text: A woman being in charge makes men apprehensive

indicators.note: apprehensive read as seizing hold of, so the words grip a woman's name between them

explanation.surface: A female boss makes the male staff nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehensive' is read as apprehending, catching hold of the name inside 'makes men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esme is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Rush — a spring flowering plant

parts.note: to speed is to rush
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A dash for a plant that blooms in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' seems to describe the season the plant flowers in; it is WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, a small blue-flowered plant.

clue.text: Cheese list-not to be used

indicators.note: to be used here means put to use in a different arrangement, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cheese list that won't be needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be used' asks for LIST-NOT to be reworked into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a strong blue English cheese.

clue.text: Encourage the serving of the currently fashionable drink

parts.note: in means in fashion now
spirit is strong alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Serving the trendiest cocktail boosts morale.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspirit is to fill with courage, to hearten.

clue.text: A countryman is able to aid an organisation

parts.note: can means is able

indicators.note: organisation as arranging, so these letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man able to help a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a native of Canada, a compatriot there.

clue.text: To take ready-prepared food into the home is most efficient

indicators.note: into means the eating word goes inside the home word

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's
to take food that is ready is to eat it

explanation.surface: Bringing a takeaway home is the most efficient way to dine.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest means tidiest and most deft, the most efficient way of doing a thing.

clue.text: Try running water

definitions.meaning: to try something out is to put it to the proof
the River ..., a chalk stream in Hampshire, England

explanation.definitionFit: To try is to examine; and the Test is a famous Hampshire trout river.

clue.text: Charge brought by firm holy man

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A firm brings a charge against a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price asked for something, its cost.

clue.text: Settle down to make music

definitions.meaning: to write a piece of music

explanation.definitionFit: Composing oneself means calming; composing a piece means writing a score.

clue.text: After a party, prudent medication is called for!

parts.note: a do is a party
sage means wise, prudent

explanation.surface: After a party, a sensible dose of medicine is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosage is the amount of medicine prescribed.

clue.text: Regret taking exercise in break

indicators.note: taking means the break word holds the exercise word inside

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Regretting the decision to exercise during a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel sorry for what one has done.

clue.text: A little cash deposited-that's material

parts.note: P is a penny, a little cash in British money
laid means put down or deposited

explanation.surface: A small sum is banked, and that's the important thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a tartan woollen cloth, a material.

clue.text: The code's a mere shop device

indicators.note: device suggests a contrivance made from these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secret code turns out to be only a shopkeeper's trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device' is the anagram signal: A MERE SHOP is contrived into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a signalling code using flags held in different positions.

clue.text: The City's into convenience food and scrap

indicators.note: into means the City's code goes inside the food word

parts.note: a pie is ready-made food
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A City financier eats convenience food and leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a fragment or scrap.

clue.text: Cavalryman capturing a forager

indicators.note: capturing means the horseman word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a cavalryman is a horse rider

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier takes a foraging enemy prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider forages, plundering supplies from enemy territory.

clue.text: Insurance too is included in the pound!

indicators.note: is included in means the word for too sits inside the pound word

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a cage
over as in excessively, too much

explanation.surface: A remark that pet insurance is also covered by the dog pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money, but here it is an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance coverage is the protection a policy provides.

clue.text: T-junction muddle

parts.note: an angle is where two lines meet, a junction

explanation.surface: A muddle at a T-junction on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a confused muddle, as of knotted threads.

clue.text: Opinion held about people being given a flat

indicators.note: held about means the opinion word is wrapped around the people word

parts.note: a tenet is a held belief or opinion
men means people

explanation.surface: A view on housing people in flats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building of rented rooms; in Scotland, one apartment within it.
